headline: Margins expand, cash flow surges as revenue outlook trims
summary_short: WM's Q2 2026 revenue rose 4.0% y/y to $6,684M, with adjusted operating EBITDA up 5.5% to $2,067M (margin +40bp to 30.9%) and adjusted EPS up 5.2% to $2.02; free cash flow jumped 34.5% to $1.10B. Full-year revenue guidance was trimmed slightly while margin guidance was raised.
summary_long: Revenue growth (+4.0% y/y) was driven by core price of 5.7% and Collection & Disposal yield of 3.6%, plus higher recycling/renewable-energy volumes and surcharges; Collection & Disposal volume fell 1.8%, largely a wildfire-cleanup comp. Flat opex ratio (59.2%) and 60bp SG&A improvement lifted adjusted EBITDA margin 40bp to 30.9%. Operating cash flow rose nearly 12% to $1.73B, driving free cash flow up 34.5% to $1.10B; WM returned $1.04B to shareholders ($659M buybacks, $379M dividends). Equity dipped 1.0% q/q on buybacks/dividends; cash ended at $557M. FY2026 outlook: EBITDA ($8.15-8.25B) and FCF ($3.75-3.85B) reaffirmed; revenue guidance cut ~0.6% to $26.275-26.475B on lower volumes; margin guidance raised 20bp to 31.0-31.2%.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites earnings growth, margin expansion, and cash flow generation reflecting consistent execution; adjusted operating EBITDA grew 5.5%, or 9.1% excluding the prior-year wildfire cleanup contribution.
Growth driven by core price of 5.7% and Collection & Disposal yield of 3.6%, plus higher recycling and renewable-energy volumes from completed growth projects and higher energy surcharges.
8.9% y/y growth roughly tracks the 5.5% adjusted EBITDA growth plus modestly higher D&A ($777M vs $744M), partly from the 2026 landfill-accretion reclassification into D&A.
Led by Collection & Disposal (+$79M adjusted) on favorable price-to-cost spread and reduced frontline turnover, plus +$40M from recycling/renewable energy and +$11M from Healthcare Solutions.
40bp adjusted expansion from a flat opex ratio despite higher fuel costs, plus a 60bp SG&A-margin improvement from cost discipline and Stericycle synergy capture.
The release attributes the 34.5% increase to operating EBITDA growth and working-capital improvements lifting operating cash flow nearly 12% to $1.73B.
Not explained in the release as a standalone line; the cash-flow statement shows $1.73B of operating cash inflow against $1.28B of capex, $85M of M&A, and $1.04B of shareholder returns.
Not explained in the release; the q/q decline is consistent with $659M of buybacks and $379M of dividends in the quarter exceeding net income retained.
